headline: GROUP ELEVEN DRILLS MASSIVE SULPHIDE 550m FROM STONEPARK RESOURCE — 14.7m at 2.0% Zn+Pb, 1m at 21.7%; Most Significant Hit Since 2017 (TSXV: ZNG)
snippet: Group Eleven Resources Corp. (TSXV: ZNG) announced July 23 that a new zone of massive to semi-massive sulphide mineralization has been discovered at its 78.62%-owned Stonepark Project in Ireland — 550 metres from the closest edge of the existing Mineral Resource Estimate — with step-out hole 26-2638-07 returning 14.7 metres at 2.0% Zn+Pb from 461 metres depth, including 2.8 metres at 8.3% Zn+Pb and 1.0 metre at 21.7% Zn+Pb. CEO Bart Jaworski called it the most significant drilling result at Stonepark since Group Eleven assumed operatorship in 2017, with follow-up drilling planned as part of a 12,800-metre campaign in late 2026 or early 2027 targeting the perceived mirror image of Glencore's Pallas Green zinc-lead deposit — adjacent to Group Eleven's own high-grade Ballywire zinc-lead-silver-germanium discovery on the south side of Ireland's Limerick Volcanic Complex.

headline: GREENLIGHT METALS DRILLS 52m AT 2.75% CuEq IN WISCONSIN VMS — 103 g/t TELLURIUM, 2.49 g/t Au; Phase 2 Extends Bend Footwall Zone 75m Down-Dip (TSXV: GRL)
snippet: GreenLight Metals Inc. (TSXV: GRL) reported July 22 assay results from its Phase 2 drill program at the Bend copper-gold VMS deposit in Taylor County, Wisconsin, with hole B26-009 intersecting 52.18 metres grading 1.12 g/t Au and 103.21 g/t tellurium (1.28% CuEq), including 10.82 metres at 2.49 g/t Au and 2.75% CuEq — extending gold-bearing sulphide mineralization approximately 75 metres down-dip from prior 2026 intercepts. The tellurium content in the footwall tuff horizon adds a critical mineral dimension to a VMS system already compelling for its copper-gold grades; GreenLight is advancing the initial ~4,000-metre portion of a permitted 7,000-metre Phase 2 program on a state-leased parcel, with additional holes in progress.

headline: PUMA EXPLORATION INAUGURAL DRILL CONFIRMS HIGH-GRADE GOLD AT McKENZIE — 42.60 g/t Au IN VEIN; 5-20m LOW-GRADE ENVELOPE; New Brunswick System Validated (TSXV: PUMA)
snippet: Puma Exploration Inc. (TSXV: PUMA) announced July 21 results from its inaugural 2,721-metre diamond drill program at the RIM Gold Zone of the McKenzie Gold Project in Northern New Brunswick, confirming high-grade vein-hosted gold within a broader 5-to-20-metre low-grade shear envelope — best vein intercepts including 42.60 g/t Au over 0.25 metres, 21.86 g/t Au over 0.30 metres, and 15.55 g/t Au over 0.30 metres. The program validates the geological model at a project where surface sampling had already returned up to 126 g/t Au, and identifies drill targets for a planned fall 2026 follow-up program — representing a meaningful derisking milestone for a district-scale gold explorer operating in one of Eastern Canada's less explored mineral belts.

headline: DISCOVERY MINING CONFIRMS LARGE-SCALE PAMOUR DEPOSIT — 64.8 Mt AT 1.30 g/t Au; 17.36 g/t Au INTERCEPTS; 4km Open-Pit System Open at Depth, Shares +8.1% (TSX: DSV)
snippet: Discovery Mining Ltd. (TSX: DSV) reported July 21 that 47 holes totalling 11,003 metres from its record 255,000–285,000-metre 2026 drill campaign confirm and expand a 4-kilometre mineralized open-pit gold system at the Pamour mine near Timmins, Ontario — hosting 64.8 Mt indicated at 1.30 g/t Au (2.70 Moz) plus 23.3 Mt inferred at 1.34 g/t Au (1.00 Moz) — with high-grade intercepts reaching 17.36 g/t Au in new targets adjacent to the existing resource. The system remains open along strike and at 300–700 metres depth; shares gained 8.1% on the announcement as the market recognizes Pamour as a credible large-tonnage open-pit gold development candidate in Ontario's Timmins camp, one of the most prolific gold districts in Canadian history.

headline: SILVER ONE RESTARTS CANDELARIA 20,000-25,000m DRILL CAMPAIGN — Major Drilling Contracted; Nevada Oxide, Mixed, Porphyry Cu-Ag-Au Targets Imminent (TSXV: SVE)
snippet: Silver One Resources Inc. (TSXV: SVE) announced July 22 that drilling will resume at its 100%-owned Candelaria Silver Project in Nevada — one of the largest undeveloped primary silver systems in North America — following a brief interruption of the program originally disclosed May 27. Major Drilling has been contracted with mobilization underway and first holes scheduled immediately upon site setup; the 20,000–25,000-metre reverse-circulation program targets resource expansion adjacent to existing silver resources, new oxide and mixed oxide-sulphide zones, and deeper porphyry-style copper-silver-gold targets identified through prior geophysical surveys — a restart signalling continued operator conviction in Candelaria's scale potential near the current $58–60 silver price.

headline: KUYA SILVER BETHANIA Q2 RECORD: 5,097 TONNES, +66% OVER Q1 — June Monthly High 13,273 AgEq Oz; Peru Underground Ramp Shows Real Production Trajectory (CSE: KUYA)
snippet: Kuya Silver Corporation (CSE: KUYA) reported July 21 a record second quarter at the Bethania underground silver mine in Peru — 5,097 metric tonnes processed, a 66% improvement over Q1 2026 and a new quarterly high — with June delivering a record daily throughput of 124 tonnes, a record monthly 2,040 tonnes (68 tpd), and a record 13,273 silver-equivalent ounces in a single month. The steady ramp positions Kuya's low-capex Peru operation to reach a meaningful annualized silver production run-rate before year-end; for investors tracking whether junior silver producers can actually deliver into the sixth consecutive annual supply deficit, Kuya's trajectory is one of the more credible real-world data points currently available.

headline: URANIUM SECTOR HEATS: KAZATOMPROM -10%, AI HYPERSCALERS SIGNING NUCLEAR PPAs, DEMAND COULD DOUBLE BY 2040 — 3 Stocks to Watch Before July's FOMC
snippet: A 24/7 Wall St. analyst review published July 23 highlights three uranium securities worth watching as structural demand signals intensify even while spot consolidates at US$84–87/lb: Kazakhstan's Kazatomprom has confirmed a 10% output cut for 2026, major AI hyperscalers continue signing long-term nuclear power purchase agreements to supply data centre baseload, and 38 countries have pledged to triple nuclear capacity by 2050 — with the World Nuclear Association projecting uranium demand potentially doubling to over 150,000 tonnes annually by 2040 against current annual mine output near 67,000 tonnes. The piece argues the July 28–29 FOMC meeting, if dovish in tone, could free up risk appetite that has kept uranium equities range-bound despite improving supply fundamentals.

headline: ALL 18 RARE EARTHS SURGE IN JULY — NdPr ALLOY +21% TO $133/KG, GERMANIUM +27.8%, DYSPROSIUM +25.4%; Average Basket Gain 16.7%; China Quota Squeeze Intensifies
snippet: Every one of 18 tracked rare earth elements rose in July 2026, led by germanium (+27.8% to ~$2,673/kg domestic China), indium (+26.5%), dysprosium (+25.4% to $261.63/kg), and NdPr alloy (+21.4% to $133.02/kg) — average basket gain of 16.7% — driven by China's smelter quota enforcement, environmental inspections, and MOFCOM export-licensing constraints. The NdPr surge is acutely relevant for EV permanent magnet producers repricing long-term off-take agreements; dysprosium's move extends the heavy rare earth crunch already tracked in Q2. With China controlling 98–99% of separated heavy rare earth output and 80% of refined germanium globally, Western semiconductor producers and defence contractors have no near-term substitution path — reinforcing the strategic case for developing independent rare earth supply chains in Canada, Australia, and Greenland.

headline: THE FED MEETS JULY 29: GOLD PRICED IN THE HOLD, SILVER IS NOT — Committee Split 9-8; No Dot Plot; Warsh's Tone Is the Only Catalyst That Matters This Week
snippet: A GoldSilver.com editorial published ahead of the July 28–29 FOMC meeting argues that gold's consolidation around $4,050–4,130 already reflects the 89% market-priced probability of an unchanged rate decision — but silver, trading near $58–60 against JPMorgan's year-end target of $81 and the LBMA analyst consensus of $79.57, has far more asymmetric upside if Fed Chair Warsh signals a September pause over a hike. The piece notes the committee is split 9-to-8 on rate increases and that July's meeting produces no dot plot or Summary of Economic Projections, making Warsh's precise language the single most important macro catalyst for precious metals over the coming week.

headline: GOLD TECHNICALLY OVERSOLD, DEBASEMENT TRADE INTACT — Sprott's Paul Wong: $5,595 January High Was Overbought; Current Correction Is a Setup, Not a Trend Reversal
snippet: Sprott Asset Management's Paul Wong told Kitco News July 20 that gold's correction from January's $5,595 all-time high to the current $4,050–4,130 range has made the metal technically oversold — noting gold peaked when overbought and has now swung to the opposite extreme — while the structural forces behind the original move remain fully intact: currency debasement, central bank reserve diversification, and chronic fiscal deficit expansion. Wong's analysis, widely syndicated July 21, distinguishes between a cyclical repricing tied to Fed rate-hike expectations and a secular trend supported by de-dollarization flows, arguing the current setup resembles prior corrective episodes that preceded the next leg of a structural bull market.
